content: 1. A double-blind, randomized, active-controlled, multicenter study was conducted and published in Nephrology Dialysis Transplantation in April 2005 (Volume 20, Issue 4, Pages 743-746). 2. Jemsek JG, Arathoon E, Arlotti M, et al. investigated the effects of atazanavir and efavirenz on body fat and other metabolic parameters when combined with zidovudine and lamivudine in antiretroviral-naive HIV-infected patients. The findings were published in Clinical Infectious Diseases on January 15, 2006 (Volume 42, Issue 2, Pages 273-280). 3. Johnson M and Moyle G reported the 96-week efficacy and safety outcomes of atazanavir/ritonavir (ATV/r) versus lopinavir/ritonavir (LPV/r) in antiretroviral-naive HIV-1-infected patients in the CASTLE study. The results were published in HIV Medicine in April 2009 (Volume 10, Page 17). 4. Kappelhoff BS, van Leth F, Robinson PA, et al. explored whether adverse events associated with nevirapine and efavirenz were related to plasma concentrations. Their study was published in Antiviral Therapy in 2005 (Volume 10, Issue 4, Pages 489-498). 5. Kozal MJ, Lupo S, DeJesus E, et al. presented the results of the SPARTAN study, which evaluated a nucleosideand ritonavir-sparing regimen containing atazanavir plus raltegravir in antiretroviral treatment-naive HIV-infected patients. The findings were published in HIV Clinical Trials in May-June 2012 (Volume 13, Issue 3, Pages 119-130). 6. Kumar P, DeJesus E, Huhn G, et al. assessed cardiovascular biomarkers in a randomized trial comparing fosamprenavir/ritonavir versus efavirenz with abacavir/lamivudine in underrepresented, antiretroviral-naive, HIV-infected patients (SUPPORT study). The 96-week results were published in BMC Infectious Diseases on June 7, 2013 (Volume 13, Article 1). 7. Kumar PN, Salvato P, LaMarca A, et al. conducted a randomized, controlled trial comparing initial antiretroviral therapy with abacavir/lamivudine/zidovudine twice daily versus atazanavir once daily with lamivudine/zidovudine twice daily in HIV-infected patients over 48 weeks (ACTION Study, ESS100327). The results were published in AIDS Research and Therapy on April 9, 2009 (Volume 6, Article 3). 8. Landman R, Koulla-Shiro S, Sow PS, et al. evaluated four tenofovir-containing regimens as first-line treatments in Cameroon and Senegal in the ANRS 12115 DAYANA trial. The findings were published in Antiviral Therapy in 2014 (Volume 19, Issue 1, Pages 51-59). 9. Lazzarin A, Orkin C, DeJesus E, et al. reported the 192-week efficacy and safety outcomes of once-daily darunavir/ritonavir (DRV/r) versus lopinavir/ritonavir (LPV/r) in treatment-naive HIV-1-infected adults in the ARTEMIS trial. The results were published in Infection in March 2011 (Volume 39, Supplement 26-27). 10. Lennox JL, DeJesus E, Berger DS, et al. published a study on the safety and efficacy of raltegravir-based versus efavirenz-based combination therapy in treatment-naive patients with HIV-1 infection. This multicenter, double-blind, randomized controlled trial was published in The Lancet on September 5, 2009 (Volume 374, Issue 9692, Pages 796-806). 11. Lennox JL, Landovitz RJ, Ribaudo HJ, et al. evaluated the efficacy and tolerability of three non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor-sparing antiretroviral regimens in treatment-naive HIV-1-infected volunteers. This randomized, controlled equivalence trial was published in Annals of Internal Medicine on October 7, 2014 (Volume 161, Issue 7, Pages 461-471). 12. Li T, Dai Y, Kuang J, et al. conducted a multicentric observational cohort study on three generic nevirapine-based antiretroviral treatments in Chinese HIV/AIDS patients. The findings were published in PLoS ONE in 2008 (Volume 3, Issue 12, Article e3918). 13. Maggiolo F, Ripamonti D, Gregis G, et al. investigated once-daily therapy for HIV infection in a controlled, randomized study involving antiretroviral-naive HIV-1-infected patients. The results were published in Antiviral Therapy in August 2003 (Volume 8, Issue 4, Pages 339-346). 14. Malan DR, Krantz E, David N, et al. reported the 96-week efficacy and safety outcomes of atazanavir, with and without ritonavir, in a HAART regimen for treatment-naive patients. The findings were published in Journal of the International Association of Physicians in AIDS Care in January-February 2010 (Volume 9, Issue 1, Pages 34-42). 15. Malan DR, Krantz E, David N, et al. also published a study on the efficacy and safety of atazanavir, with or without ritonavir, as part of once-daily highly active antiretroviral therapy regimens in antiretroviral-naive patients. This study appeared in Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes on February 1, 2008 (Volume 47, Issue 2, Pages 161-167). 16. Malan N, Su J, Mancini M, et al. analyzed gastrointestinal tolerability and quality of life in antiretroviral-naive HIV-1-infected patients using data from the CASTLE study. The findings were published in AIDS Care in June 2010 (Volume 22, Issue 6, Pages 677-686). 17. Markowitz M, Nguyen BY, Gotuzzo E, et al. demonstrated the sustained antiretroviral effect of raltegravir after 96 weeks of combination therapy in treatment-naive patients with HIV-1 infection. The results were published in Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes on November 1, 2009 (Volume 52, Issue 3, Pages 350-356). 18. Markowitz M, Nguyen BY, Gotuzzo E, et al. also reported the rapid and durable antiretroviral effect of the HIV-1 integrase inhibitor raltegravir as part of combination therapy in treatment-naive patients with HIV-1 infection. The 48-week controlled study results were published in Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes on October 1, 2007 (Volume 46, Issue 2, Pages 125-133). 19. Martinez E, Gonzalez-Cordon A, Ferrer E, et al. investigated early lipid changes associated with atazanavir/ritonavir or darunavir/ritonavir. The findings were published in HIV Medicine in July 2014 (Volume 15, Issue 6, Pages 330-338). 20. Martinez E, Gonzalez-Cordon A, Ferrer E, et al. also studied the differential body composition effects of protease inhibitors recommended for initial treatment of HIV infection in a randomized clinical trial. The results were published in Clinical Infectious Diseases on March 1, 2015 (Volume 60, Issue 5, Pages 811-820).
